citation: Iwabe et al. 2025. Slow-paced breathing reduces anxiety and enhances midfrontal alpha asymmetry, buffering responses to aversive visual stimuli. Frontiers in Human Neuroscience
protocol: Resting natural breathing (RB) block in a reclined chair, 17 healthy students; slow-paced breathing block for comparison; EEG and respiration recorded
population: 17 healthy students (7 F, 10 M), mean age 22.2 y
note: Mean 14.76 with SD 3.43 for the natural-breathing block, from text. Reclined chair (seated/reclining posture stated). Duration of the resting block not checked.
